title: Towards Robust Information Extraction via Binomial Distribution Guided Counterpart Sequence

problem.claim: Information extraction aims to extract meaningful structured tuples from unstructured text.

gap.claim: Existing evaluation metrics treat a slight tuple error as complete prediction failure, and prior work has ignored semantic uncertainty during target-sequence generation.

contributions.claim: The work proposes Matching Score to evaluate predicted-tuple correctness in more detail.
The work proposes the model-agnostic Binomial distribution guided counterpart sequence method.

The method quantifies local semantic uncertainties over the whole sequence, formulates a binomial distribution for each local decoding step, samples a counterpart sequence, and aligns target and counterpart semantics with Kullback-Leibler divergence.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe Matching Score as a novel information-extraction evaluation metric.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Extensive experiments on 14 public datasets covering 5 information-extraction tasks demonstrate the effectiveness of the approach across various methods, according to the authors.
The authors report that their code and dataset are available.

narrative_sequence.summary: Information extraction extracts structured tuples from unstructured text, commonly using pretrained generative language models to rephrase sentences into target sequences.
Tuple-level evaluation can treat slight errors as total failures, while semantic uncertainty in sequence generation has been overlooked.
The proposed model-agnostic BCS method uses sequence-level semantic uncertainty and Matching Score to construct local binomial distributions and sample semantic-complement counterpart sequences.
The method aligns the semantics of target and counterpart sequences using Kullback-Leibler divergence.
The authors report experiments across 14 public datasets and 5 information-extraction tasks, along with code and dataset availability.

source_observation.claim: A tuple-level metric that accounts for partial correctness is proposed because slight tuple errors are otherwise treated as complete failures.

interpretation.claim: Evaluation can become more informative when it measures the extent of structured-output correctness rather than only exact success.

application.claim: Use partial-credit evaluation for structured prediction tasks where local errors differ in severity.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify when partial-credit evaluation may be inappropriate or how Matching Score behaves across error types.

source_observation.claim: The method uses built-in language-model semantic uncertainty to sample a counterpart sequence and align it with the target sequence.

interpretation.claim: Model uncertainty can be used as a training signal or augmentation source for improving robustness.

application.claim: In generative structured prediction, construct uncertainty-informed alternative sequences and align their semantics with the intended output.

exception.claim: The abstract does not identify which uncertainty estimates are reliable or when counterpart sequences may introduce harmful semantic variation.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the 14 datasets, 5 tasks, baseline methods, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not define the Matching Score formula or the binomial-distribution construction details.
The abstract does not report limitations, computational costs, or failure cases.
